title: Sensex Falls 1,300 Points, Nifty Below 22,250 as Global Tensions Shake Indian Markets
text:
Mumbai, India — April 2, 2026
Indian equity markets witnessed a sharp sell-off on Thursday, with benchmark indices tumbling amid weak global cues and rising geopolitical tensions.
The BSE Sensex plunged more than 1,300 points during intraday trade, while the Nifty 50 slipped below the crucial 22,250 mark, erasing gains made in the previous session.
Broad-Based Selling Across Sectors
The market decline was led by heavy selling in banking and pharmaceutical stocks, which dragged the indices lower. Investors remained cautious as volatility increased across sectors.
Market participants reported widespread profit booking along with risk-off sentiment, contributing to the steep fall.
Global Tensions Weigh on Sentiment
Investor sentiment was significantly impacted by escalating geopolitical tensions, particularly developments related to the ongoing conflict between the United States and Iran.
Recent remarks by U.S. President Donald Trump added to uncertainty, triggering nervousness across global markets and influencing domestic equities.
Nifty Slides After Previous Gains
After posting gains in the previous session, the Nifty reversed sharply, falling below 22,250 as selling pressure intensified through the trading day.
Analysts noted that the sudden reversal highlights fragile market sentiment and sensitivity to global developments.
Banking and Pharma Stocks Lead Decline
Banking stocks, often considered market heavyweights, were among the worst hit, along with pharmaceutical companies. The sectoral weakness amplified losses in benchmark indices.
Traders indicated that foreign institutional investor (FII) activity and global cues played a key role in the downturn.
Market Outlook
Experts suggest that markets may remain volatile in the near term as geopolitical uncertainties continue to unfold. Investors are advised to remain cautious and monitor global developments closely.
